title: Rigveda 1.90: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.90: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.90 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 61r-61v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.90.1-4 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 17); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 61r
translation.original_text:
1ṛ̱ju̱nī̱tī no̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro na̍yatu vi̱dvān | a̱rya̱mā de̱vaiḥ sa̱joṣā̍ḥ ||
2te hi vasvo̱ vasa̍vānā̱s te apra̍mūrā̱ maho̍bhiḥ | vra̱tā ra̍kṣante vi̱śvāhā̍ ||
3te a̱smabhya̱ṁ śarma̍ yaṁsann a̱mṛtā̱ martye̍bhyaḥ | bādha̍mānā̱ apa̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
4vi na̍ḥ pa̱thaḥ su̍vi̱tāya̍ ci̱yantv indro̍ ma̱ruta̍ḥ | pū̱ṣā bhago̱ vandyā̍saḥ ||
translation.text:
1MAY Varuṇa with guidance straight, and Mitra lead us, he who knows, And Aryaman in accord with Gods.
2For they are dealers forth of wealth, and, not deluded, with their might Guard evermore the holy laws.
3Shelter may they vouchsafe to us, Immortal Gods to mortal men, Chasing our enemies away.
4May they mark out our paths to bliss, Indra, the Maruts, Pûshan, and Bhaga, the Gods to be adored.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 61r (OPenn image 62, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.89.7 ‹-sūra-cakṣasaḥ viśve naḥ devāḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 61v, begins in RV 1.90.5 ‹uta naḥ dhiyaḥ go--agrāḥ›. Verses 1.90.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1ṛju-nītī | naḥ | varuṇaḥ | mitraḥ | nayatu | vidvān | aryamā | devaiḥ | sa-joṣāḥ
2te | hi | vasvaḥ | vasavānāḥ | te | apra-mūrāḥ | mahaḥ-bhiḥ | vratā | rakṣante | viśvāhā
3te | asmabhyam | śarma | yaṃsan | amṛtāḥ | martyebhyaḥ | bādhamānāḥ | apa | dviṣaḥ
4vi | naḥ | pathaḥ | suvitāya | ciyantu | indraḥ | marutaḥ | pūṣā | bhagaḥ | vandyāsaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 1.90.5-9 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 17); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 61v
translation.original_text:
5u̱ta no̱ dhiyo̱ goa̍grā̱ḥ pūṣa̱n viṣṇa̱v eva̍yāvaḥ | kartā̍ naḥ svasti̱mata̍ḥ ||
6madhu̱ vātā̍ ṛtāya̱te madhu̍ kṣaranti̱ sindha̍vaḥ | mādhvī̍r naḥ sa̱ntv oṣa̍dhīḥ ||
7madhu̱ nakta̍m u̱toṣaso̱ madhu̍ma̱t pārthi̍va̱ṁ raja̍ḥ | madhu̱ dyaur a̍stu naḥ pi̱tā ||
8madhu̍mān no̱ vana̱spati̱r madhu̍mām̐ astu̱ sūrya̍ḥ | mādhvī̱r gāvo̍ bhavantu naḥ ||
9śaṁ no̍ mi̱traḥ śaṁ varu̍ṇa̱ḥ śaṁ no̍ bhavatv arya̱mā | śaṁ na̱ indro̱ bṛha̱spati̱ḥ śaṁ no̱ viṣṇu̍r urukra̱maḥ ||
translation.text:
5Yea, Pûshan, Vishṇu, ye who run your course, enrich our hymns with kine; Bless us with all prosperity.
6The winds waft sweets, the rivers pour sweets for the man who keeps the Law So may the plants be sweet for us.
7Sweet be the night and sweet the dawns, sweet the terrestrial atmosphere; Sweet be our Father Heaven to us.
8May the tall tree be full of sweets for us, and full of sweets the Sun: May our milch-kine be sweet for us.
9Be Mitra gracious unto us, and Varuṇa and Aryaman: Indra, Br̥ihaspati be kind, and Vishṇu of the mighty stride.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 61v (OPenn image 63, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.90.5 ‹uta naḥ dhiyaḥ go--agrāḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 62r, begins in RV 1.91.3 ‹-asi soma›. Verses 1.90.5-9 end on this page.

6madhu | vātāḥ | ṛtayate | madhu | kṣaranti | sindhavaḥ | mādhvīḥ | naḥ | santu | oṣadhīḥ
7madhu | naktam | uta | uṣasaḥ | madhu-mat | pārthivam | rajaḥ | madhu | dyauḥ | astu | naḥ | pitā
8madhu-mān | naḥ | vanaspatiḥ | madhu-mān | astu | sūryaḥ | mādhvīḥ | gāvaḥ | bhavantu | naḥ
